title: Stellus Capital Investment Corporation Announces $0.34 First Quarter 2026 Regular Dividend, Payable Monthly in Increments of $0.1133 in February, March, and April 2026
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Stellus Capital Investment Corporation's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: Press Release View printer-friendly version << Back Stellus Capital Investment Corporation Announces $0.34 First Quarter 2026 Regular Dividend, Payable Monthly in Increments of $0.1133 in February, March, and April 2026 January 16, 2026 at 5:37 PM EST HOUSTON , Jan. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stellus Capital Investment Corporation (the "Company") (NYSE: SCM) announced that its Board of Directors has declared a monthly dividend of $0.1133 for each of January, February, and March, totaling $0.34 per share in the aggregate for the first quarter of 2026. The regular dividend of $0.34 per share will be paid to shareholders of record in February, March, and April 2026. Robert T. Ladd, Chief Executive Officer of the Company, stated, "The reduction in our regular dividend in the first quarter reflects the lower interest rate environment." title: Falcon v1.3 is live!
summary: We shipped Falcon v1.3 with streaming voice cloning and faster time-to-first-translation for smoother live conversations.
body_text: Falcon v1.3 - a new iteration of our translation model at Pinch. What’s new in v1.3: Real-time voice cloning (streaming): the translation can speak in your voice - adapting tone + timbre on the fly while you’re talking. Voice cloning is often done by recording a sample of your voice from 5-30 seconds to use as a reference. With our Falcon model, we handle partial voice references naturally and perform streaming voice cloning. We do this by dynamically capturing fingerprints of your voice while you speak. From that fingerprint, Falcon can output translations with your speaker identity - capturing things like timbre and pitch tendencies. The goal is to keep the speaker’s voice characteristics consistent but adaptive, even when the spoken words are different. Faster TTFT (time-to-first-translation): language-specific improvements that reduce latency and make interim / partial speech behave better, so live conversations feel smoother. TTFT is not just about raw inference speed - it’s about when the system is confident enough to start speaking. In streaming translation, early audio is often ambiguous, and many systems wait too long before committing, which makes conversations feel turn-based even if total latency is low. In Falcon v1.3, we optimized for early, partial commitment. The model is trained to emit useful intermediate translations sooner, while remaining rewrite stable as more context arrives. The result is a system that feels responsive in real conversations - especially when paired with real-time voice cloning, where latency is much more perceptible. Live translation shouldn’t feel like a separate narrator interrupting you. It should feel like you - just multilingual.

title: What to Do When a Contractor Ghosts You Mid-Project
summary: Three weeks into a rebrand, my designer stopped replying. No warning. No "hey, something came up." Just silence.
body_text: Three weeks into a rebrand, my designer stopped replying. No warning. No "hey, something came up." Just silence. Her last message was a thumbs-up emoji on a Monday. By Thursday I was refreshing my inbox like a jilted ex. She had all the source files. Half the deliverables were done. And I had no backup plan because I never thought I needed one. If you work with contractors long enough, this will happen to you. Not might. Will. Here is what I have learned about handling it, preventing it, and building systems so it does not wreck your timeline when it does. First 48 hours: do not panic, but do act fast When a contractor goes quiet, your first instinct is to wait. Give them a day. People get sick. Phones break. Life happens. Give them 24 hours, then send a clear message: "Hey, haven't heard from you since Monday. Are you okay? Need to know if you're still able to continue this project." Direct. Not passive-aggressive. Not apologetic. Just clear. If another 24 hours passes with nothing, you are being ghosted. Accept it and move to damage control. The mistake most people make is waiting a week "to be respectful." A week is eternity when you have a launch date. Respect is a two-way street, and someone who disappears without a word has already broken that contract. Secure what you have Before you do anything else, lock down the work that exists. This means: Download every file, design, code commit, or document they have shared so far Check shared drives, repos, and project management tools for anything in progress Revoke access to sensitive systems if they had any Document exactly what was delivered and what is still missing With my designer, I got lucky. She had been uploading to a shared Figma. I had most of the in-progress work. But I have heard horror stories of people whose contractor had everything on a local machine and just vanished with it. If your work lives on someone else's hard drive and they disappear, you have nothing. Keep that in mind for next time. Figure out what you owe (and what you do not) This is where things get awkward. You hired someone. They did some work. They disappeared. Do you pay for the partial work? My take: yes, if the work is usable. No, if it is not. If they completed 60% of the deliverables and you can actually use that 60%, pay for it. Pro-rate the agreed amount. Send the payment with a note explaining the calculation. Be fair even when you are frustrated. If they delivered nothing usable, you do not owe anything. This is why milestone-based payments exist. If you paid everything upfront and got ghosted mid-project, that is an expensive lesson in payment structure. We built Grade partly because of situations like this. When payments are tied to verified deliverables, ghosting does not mean you lose money on unfinished work. You pay for what was actually done. Finding a replacement without starting over The panic move is posting on Upwork with "URGENT" in the title. Do not do this. Desperate hiring leads to desperate choices. Instead, look at who you already know. Previous contractors who did good work. People in your network. Someone who already understands your product or industry. Cold-starting with a stranger on an urgent timeline is the worst-case scenario. When you bring someone new in, give them the honest picture: "Our previous contractor left mid-project. Here is what is done. Here is what is left. Here is the timeline. Can you do it?" Good contractors appreciate honesty. Bad ones will say yes to anything. One thing that saved me: having documentation. Not just the deliverables, but notes on decisions made, brand guidelines, technical specs. The new designer did not have to guess what the old one was thinking because I had written it down. Why contractors ghost (it is usually not malicious) I eventually heard from my designer. Three weeks later. She had a family emergency and was embarrassed about going silent. By the time she felt ready to explain, she was too ashamed to reach out. That is the most common reason, honestly. It is rarely "I took your money and ran." It is usually some combination of: They got overwhelmed and did not know how to say so A personal crisis hit and work fell off their radar They took on too many projects and yours got deprioritized They realized they were in over their head and froze instead of admitting it Understanding this does not fix the problem, but it changes how you prevent it. The solution is not finding "more reliable people." It is building systems that catch silence early. How to ghost-proof your contractor relationships After getting burned, I changed how I work with contractors. Not dramatically. Just a few things that make ghosting less likely and less damaging when it happens. Set up regular check-ins. Not daily standups. That is micromanagement. But a weekly "here is where I am, here is what is next" message keeps both sides honest. If someone misses two check-ins, you know something is wrong before the project derails. Use milestone payments, not lump sums. Break the project into chunks. Pay after each chunk. This protects you from paying for unfinished work and gives the contractor regular wins. People are less likely to disappear when they are three days away from a payment. Keep all work in shared systems. Code goes in your repo. Designs go in your Figma. Documents go in your drive. Nothing should live exclusively on someone else's machine. Have a backup. Not a full second contractor on standby. Just know who you would call. Keep a short list of people who could step in with a week's notice. When you need this list, you will be glad it exists. Make it safe to say "I'm struggling." The reason most contractors ghost instead of communicating is that they are afraid of the reaction. Tell people upfront: "If you are falling behind or something comes up, just tell me. I would rather adjust the timeline than find out by silence." It happened to me, it will happen to you Working with contractors means accepting some level of unpredictability. You are not their employer. You do not control their schedule, their life, or their other commitments. That is the tradeoff for the flexibility and cost savings that contractors offer. The goal is not to eliminate ghosting. It is to make it survivable. Milestone payments so you do not lose money. Shared systems so you do not lose work. Documentation so you do not lose context. And a short list of backups so you do not lose time. My rebrand shipped two weeks late. The new designer did solid work. And I never heard from the original designer again after her apology message. No hard feelings. Just a lesson I only needed to learn once.

title: Rinsed Launches New Quarterly Car Wash Industry Report with Insights from 2025Q4
summary: January 26, 2026 – New York, NY – Rinsed has released its latest Quarterly Car Wash Industry Report, offering new insights drawn from aggregated data across more than 3,000 car wash locations for 2025Q4.
body_text: January 26, 2026 – New York, NY – Rinsed has released its latest Quarterly Car Wash Industry Report, offering new insights drawn from aggregated data across more than 3,000 car wash locations for 2025Q4. In 2025Q4, total same-store sales revenue grew 4.8% year-over-year. While not a breakout quarter, this result reflects steady growth against a notably strong comparison period in 2024Q4, when the industry delivered exceptional performance. Membership revenue increased 11.3% year-over-year and once again served as the primary driver of total revenue growth. Retail revenue, by contrast, declined 8.4% year-over-year, highlighting the ongoing volatility of retail revenue relative to the more stable membership revenue. Broader consumer sentiment may be contributing to this dynamic, as confidence levels have fallen meaningfully compared to a year ago, often leading consumers to be more cautious with discretionary spending. The report also examines operators’ success in converting retail customers into members, broken out by average active monthly members per site. In 2025Q4, car washes with more than 4,000 members converted at 15.6%, locations with 2,000–4,000 members converted at 10.3%, and locations with fewer than 2,000 members converted just under 3%. These results continue to show that larger, more mature membership programs convert at significantly higher rates. New to this quarter’s report is a deeper look at the composition of new membership signups. In 2025Q4, over 70% of new memberships came from first-time members, while 29.2% were former members reactivating their subscriptions. This indicates that nearly three in ten new signups are win-backs, underscoring the importance of reactivation and churn-recovery campaigns as a meaningful pathway to membership growth. Churn remained stable in 2025Q4. Voluntary churn averaged 4.6%, credit card churn averaged 3.0%, and total churn averaged 7.6%. These figures are consistent with recent quarters, suggesting churn levels have largely stabilized. To view the full report and stay up to date with the latest car wash industry trends, subscribe at www.rinsed.com/subscribe . About Rinsed Rinsed integrates directly with your POS, giving you the tools to grow memberships, reduce churn, and keep customers coming back. For more information, visit www.rinsed.com
